gen-dafont-dogica-satoshi: Dogica is blocky and heavy, with lowercase that climbs nearly to the capitals. Satoshi follows in a sans with a soaring x-height and an open e, every stroke cut to one width, so long paragraphs would move along smoothly.
gen-gf-metamorphous-archivo: Archivo reads tall and approachable, its curves opening outward. Metamorphous sits above it with generous sidebearings and soft, etched-glass shifts in stroke weight, giving the page an ornamental top and a sturdy, editorial floor.
gen-gf-metamorphous-fs-asap: Asap has a body height that nearly matches its capitals, and its c forms read as open arcs. Metamorphous leads with joins that thin gently without turning spindly, so a long passage would feel sturdy underneath and decorative on top.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-switzer: Pixel-toy swagger on top, wire-thin calm underneath: Early GameBoy stretches out with modest thick-thin shifts and a skyward x-height line. Switzer, a plain sans, simply stays tubular and tidy.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-work-sans: Work Sans reads modern and sturdy, its c tips never creeping toward touching and its mean line set high. Electroharmonix breaks every word into single, spaced letters, which is the loudest thing here.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-fs-merriweather-: Fast, aggressive, and pushed wide: Ethnocentric has short ascenders above big bowls and loose tracking. Merriweather Sans does the opposite job, with tall lowercase that makes words look sturdy and an e that opens clearly to the right.
gen-dafont-groovy-fs-supreme: Funky and loosely tracked, Groovy nearly closes its c into a narrow slit while its arms and legs keep a constant width. Supreme sits below as crisp, open sans-serif.
gen-dafont-impact-label-fs-epilogue: Commanding letters stand apart like beads on a rod, each c opening its ends like pincers in Impact Label. Epilogue is a wire-like monoline sans with tall bodies; giving it a bit more size than usual would suit.
gen-dafont-joystix-switzer: Bold arcade lettering with widely tracked letters defines Joystix, its stems only a shade heavier than the arms between them. Switzer, a plain sans, bends like wire sign lettering at constant thickness.
gen-dafont-junegull-general-sans: Junegull brings retro friendliness, with lowercase as sturdy as cast iron capitals and a pinched gap at each curve's mouth. General Sans smooths out every bend with steady pen pressure, and a slightly generous size would let its tall x-height fill the line.
